phillips_1997.cite: Phillips SM, Tipton KD, Aarsland A, Wolf SE, Wolfe RR (1997). Mixed muscle protein synthesis and breakdown after resistance exercise in humans. Am J Physiol 273(1 Pt1):E99-107.
phillips_1997.numbers: FSR above rest: 3h=+112%, 24h=+65%, 48h=+34% (all P<0.01). FBR above rest: 3h=+31%(P<0.05), 24h=+18%(P<0.05), back to baseline by 48h. Net balance significant vs zero at all 4 timepoints (rest,3h,24h,48h), P<0.05. FSR-FBR correlation r=0.88,P<0.001. No difference concentric vs eccentric.

bodine_2001_ncb.cite: Bodine SC, Stitt TN, Gonzalez M, et al (2001). Akt/mTOR pathway is a crucial regulator of skeletal muscle hypertrophy and can prevent muscle atrophy in vivo. Nat Cell Biol 3(11):1014-9.
bodine_2001_ncb.n: NR (rat, multiple in vivo hypertrophy+atrophy models)
bodine_2001_ncb.numbers: Rapamycin blocked hypertrophy in ALL models tested, no atrophy in controls. Calcineurin pathway NOT activated during hypertrophy; cyclosporin A and FK506 did NOT blunt hypertrophy (forced adversary falls). Genetic Akt/mTOR activation sufficient for hypertrophy + atrophy-prevention; genetic blockade blocked hypertrophy.

drummond_2009.cite: Drummond MJ, Fry CS, Glynn EL, et al (2009). Rapamycin administration in humans blocks the contraction-induced increase in skeletal muscle protein synthesis. J Physiol 587(Pt7):1535-46.
drummond_2009.numbers: Rapamycin blocked early(1-2h) ~40% contraction-induced MPS increase. S6K1(Thr421/Ser424) phospho +6-fold in control, unchanged with rapamycin. eEF2(Thr56) phospho -25% post-exercise in control, unaltered with rapamycin (elongation inhibited). Rapamycin also blocked ERK1/2(Thr202/Tyr204) phospho increase, blunted MNK1 increase; eIF4E(Ser209) phospho unaffected (P>0.05) -- authors read as indirect/crosstalk, not direct MAPK inhibition.

schoenfeld_2017.cite: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW (2017). Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Sports Sci 35(11):1073-82.
schoenfeld_2017.numbers: Continuous weekly-sets model: P=0.002, +0.023 ES/set = +0.37% muscle-size gain/set. 2-level categorical (lower vs higher volume): P=0.03, ES diff 0.241 = 3.9 percentage-point gain difference. 3-level categorical (<5, 5-9, 10+ sets/muscle/wk): TREND ONLY, P=0.074 (not significant at conventional threshold, disclosed).

west_2009_acute.cite: West DW, Kujbida GW, Moore DR, et al (2009). Resistance exercise-induced increases in putative anabolic hormones do not enhance muscle protein synthesis or intracellular signalling in young men. J Physiol 587(Pt21):5239-47.
west_2009_acute.numbers: T/GH P<0.001, IGF-1 P<0.05 elevated in HH only, unchanged in LH. MPS(%/h): rest=0.040+/-0.007, LH=0.071+/-0.008, HH=0.064+/-0.014; exercise effect P<0.05, hormone effect P=0.72 (HH numerically LOWER than LH). p70S6K phospho increased with exercise, no between-condition difference.

west_2010_causal.cite: West DW, Burd NA, Tang JE, et al (2010). Elevations in ostensibly anabolic hormones with resistance exercise enhance neither training-induced muscle hypertrophy nor strength of the elbow flexors. J Appl Physiol 108(1):60-7.
west_2010_causal.numbers: 15wk training, LH vs HH (contralateral arms). Hormone elevation confirmed P<0.001 in HH only, maintained late vs early in training period. CSA +12%(LH) vs +10%(HH), training effect P<0.001, condition x training interaction P=0.25 (NS). Type I (P<0.01) and type II (P<0.001) fiber CSA both increased, no hormone effect on either. Strength increased both arms, no between-condition difference (exact % not given in abstract -- honest gap).

west_phillips_2012.cite: West DW, Phillips SM (2012). Associations of exercise-induced hormone profiles and gains in strength and hypertrophy in a large cohort after weight training. Eur J Appl Physiol 112(7):2693-702.
west_phillips_2012.numbers: No significant correlations: GH/fT/IGF-1 AUC vs LBM or leg-press-strength gain. Significant: cortisol AUC vs LBM change r=0.29(P<0.05); cortisol AUC vs typeII fiber CSA r=0.35(P<0.01); GH AUC vs typeI fiber CSA r=0.36(P=0.006); GH AUC vs typeII fiber CSA r=0.28(P=0.04), NOT lean mass. No hormone correlated with strength.

west_phillips_2010_review.cite: West DW, Phillips SM (2010). Anabolic processes in human skeletal muscle: restoring the identities of growth hormone and testosterone. Phys Sportsmed 38(3):97-104.
west_phillips_2010_review.numbers: Verbatim: 'GH...is not anabolic toward the contractile (ie, myofibrillar) muscle tissue in healthy individuals.' 'no evidence that transient exercise-induced changes in GH have the same effects' as clinical GH-deficiency replacement. 'exercise-induced increases in GH and testosterone availability are not necessary for and do not enhance strength and hypertrophy adaptations.' 'local mechanisms...are predominant in stimulating anabolism.'

cuthbertson_2005.cite: Cuthbertson D, Smith K, Babraj J, et al (2005). Anabolic signaling deficits underlie amino acid resistance of wasting, aging muscle. FASEB J 19(3):422-4.
cuthbertson_2005.numbers: Basal MPS indistinguishable young vs old. EAA-stimulated MPS sensitivity/responsiveness reduced in elderly, linked to decreased expression+activation(phosphorylation) of mTOR, p70S6k, eIF4BP-1, eIF2B after EAA. Effects independent of insulin (plasma insulin clamped at basal). Increased NFkB associated with the anabolic deficits.

mccarthy_2011.cite: McCarthy JJ, Mula J, Miyazaki M, et al (2011). Effective fiber hypertrophy in satellite cell-depleted skeletal muscle. Development 138(17):3657-66.
mccarthy_2011.numbers: 2wk plantaris synergist-ablation overload: satellite-cell-depleted muscle showed SAME (~2-fold) mass+fiber-CSA hypertrophy as vehicle controls. Typical myonuclei increase ABSENT (myonuclear domain expanded instead), confirmed via reduced BrdU+ myonuclei (long-term labeling). Single-fiber specific force/Ca2+ sensitivity/cross-bridge cycling unchanged. Fiber hyperplasia + regeneration (small component) significantly blunted.

egner_2016.cite: Egner IM, Bruusgaard JC, Gundersen K (2016). Satellite cell depletion prevents fiber hypertrophy in skeletal muscle. Development 143(16):2898-906.
egner_2016.n: mouse, same general Pax7-based genetic strategy as McCarthy 2011
egner_2016.numbers: Repeating McCarthy 2011's protocol with immunohistochemistry + in vivo/ex vivo imaging: overload hypertrophy PREVENTED in satellite-cell-deficient mice, both plantaris AND EDL. Attributes McCarthy's contrary finding to (a) reliance on muscle MASS as a fiber-hypertrophy proxy, (b) inclusion of a significant number of REGENERATING fibers in the analysis. Verbatim: 'there is currently no model in which functional, sustainable hypertrophy has been unequivocally demonstrated in the absence of satellite cells.'

burd_2010.cite: Burd NA, Holwerda AM, Selby KC, et al (2010). Resistance exercise volume affects myofibrillar protein synthesis and anabolic signalling molecule phosphorylation in young men. J Physiol 588(Pt16):3119-30.
burd_2010.numbers: 1SET fed-state MPS: 2.3-fold above rest at 5h, returned to resting levels by 29h. 3SET: 3.1-fold above rest at 5h (bigger amplitude), 2.3-fold above rest at 29h (longer duration). p70S6K phosphorylation correlated with MPS response, r=0.338, P=0.033. 3SET showed greater eIF2B and rpS6 activation at 5h Fed vs 1SET; p90RSK/rpS6 similar at 24h Fast/29h Fed.

ahtiainen_2003.cite: Ahtiainen JP, Pakarinen A, Alen M, Kraemer WJ, Hakkinen K (2003). Muscle hypertrophy, hormonal adaptations and strength development during strength training in strength-trained and untrained men. Eur J Appl Physiol 89(6):555-63.
ahtiainen_2003.numbers: 21wk training. NA gained MORE than SA: force +20.9%(NA) vs +3.9%(SA); CSA +5.6%(NA) vs -1.8%(SA). No significant change in basal hormones over 21wk in either group. Basal-T-mean(wk0,7,14,21) vs Disometric-force correlated r=0.84,P<0.01 in SA. Acute-DeltaT-response(wk0 vs wk21) vs Delta-CSA correlated r=0.76,P<0.05 in NA. FORCED ADVERSARY for the hormone-hypothesis refutation -- correlational, small n=8/subgroup, plausible ~12 hormone x outcome x subgroup comparisons with only 2 reported significant (multiple-comparisons concern disclosed not resolved), opposite-direction CSA/force response between subgroups on the identical protocol.

bodine_2001_science_atrogin.cite: Bodine SC, Latres E, Baumhueter S, et al (2001). Identification of ubiquitin ligases required for skeletal muscle atrophy. Science 294(5547):1704-8.
bodine_2001_science_atrogin.n: rat (transcript profiling, multiple atrophy models) + mouse (KO)
bodine_2001_science_atrogin.numbers: Transcript profiling across multiple rat atrophy models found only a small universal subset of upregulated genes; 2 are ubiquitin ligases: MuRF1 and MAFbx(atrogin-1, SCF-family E3). MAFbx overexpression in myotubes produced atrophy (sufficiency). Mice deficient in either MAFbx or MuRF1 were resistant to atrophy (necessity).

falsifier_1_mtorc1_necessity.pre_registered_threshold: rapamycin BLOCKS (not merely attenuates) the load-induced MPS increase in >=1 human RCT AND blocks hypertrophy in >=1 animal causal (loss-of-function AND gain-of-function) study spanning multiple hypertrophy-induction models, with the strongest rival pathway (calcineurin/NFAT) directly tested and falling in the same experiments
falsifier_1_mtorc1_necessity.adversary_outcome: FALLS -- cyclosporin A and FK506 did not blunt hypertrophy in the same Bodine 2001 models where rapamycin blocked it; calcineurin pathway not even activated during hypertrophy in vivo
decorrelation_axes: phenotype (hypertrophy/atrophy vs lifespan, via sibling node MOL-MTORC1-NUTRIENT-SIGNALING)
falsifier_1_mtorc1_necessity.diverse_instance_space: multiple hypertrophy models + multiple atrophy models (Bodine 2001 NCB) + human pharmacology (Drummond 2009) + decorrelated lifespan phenotype (Harrison 2009 / Miller 2011, read-only)

falsifier_2_hormone_hypothesis.pre_registered_threshold_for_adversary_s: a genuine CAUSAL/manipulated experiment holding local mechanical stimulus constant while varying systemic hormone exposure must show significant, directionally-consistent enhancement of hypertrophy/strength/MPS/signalling in the high-hormone condition
falsifier_2_hormone_hypothesis.forced_adversary_primary: the systemic-hormone-surge-drives-hypertrophy hypothesis itself, tested at its strongest (causal, manipulated) form
falsifier_2_hormone_hypothesis.adversary_outcome_primary: FALLS -- West 2010 (PMID 19910330): CSA +12%(LH) vs +10%(HH), interaction P=0.25, point estimate reversed from predicted direction; West 2009 acute MPS/signalling also null, P=0.72
falsifier_2_hormone_hypothesis.forced_adversary_secondary: independent-lab (Ahtiainen 2003, Finland, fully decorrelated from the McMaster/Phillips group behind every other hormone citation) correlational T-outcome relationships
falsifier_2_hormone_hypothesis.adversary_outcome_secondary: SURVIVES PARTIALLY -- correlational trait-level signal in small subgroups (n=8 each), does not overturn the causal test (no local-stimulus control, small-n multiple-comparisons concern disclosed not resolved, opposite-direction CSA/force response between subgroups)
falsifier_2_hormone_hypothesis.verdict: ADVERSARY FALLS on its pre-registered CAUSAL threshold (PASS for the refutation); a weaker correlational/trait-level residual (Ahtiainen 2003 subgroup correlations; West & Phillips 2012's own weak GH/cortisol-vs-fiber-CSA correlations, r=0.28-0.36) is explicitly left OPEN, not force-closed
falsifier_2_hormone_hypothesis.common_mode_risk_disclosed: 4 of 5 primary hormone-hypothesis citations (West 2009, West 2010, West-Phillips 2012, West-Phillips 2010 review) share one lab (McMaster/Phillips) -- Ahtiainen 2003 was specifically sought to decorrelate this and is the only non-McMaster hormone citation in this document
